principles.statement: Apply obligations from actual project capabilities and transitions; record every disposition explicitly.
Separate presence, syntax, semantic adequacy, and exercised runtime evidence; no layer implies a later one.
Prefer the smallest owned mechanism that closes a consequential failure path; reuse adequate signals and platforms.

Not-assessed work remains pending and non-pass. Not-applicable decisions and temporary exceptions require a separately reviewed owner decision, a bounded reason, and a substitute or residual-risk statement.

obligations.title: Executable change path
obligations.applies_when: The repository is expected to be changed or released.
required_evidence: A fresh authorized actor exercises the core user outcome or consumer contract.
The evidence distinguishes success from plausible failure and records cleanup or isolation boundaries.
obligations.exception_authority: Accountable project owner; security or data owner also approves when access or private data is involved.

obligations.title: Consequential checks and recovery
obligations.applies_when: A repeatable defect, unsafe transition, or release path exists.
required_evidence: Executable negative controls reject the named failure class.
The same path accepts a valid case, and the recovery or rollback procedure is exercised where consequential.
obligations.exception_authority: Accountable project owner with a time-bounded substitute control and residual-risk statement.

obligations.title: Safe transition and artifact identity
obligations.applies_when: A host, deployment, database, identity, realtime, or job boundary changes.
required_evidence: The exact candidate artifact and target environment are identified.
Migration, authorization, exposure, lifetime, rollback, and operator ownership are addressed without treating a proposal as deployment proof.
obligations.exception_authority: Accountable project owner and owner of every changed persistence, identity, or hosting boundary.

obligations.title: Structured diagnostics and errors
obligations.applies_when: Code operates asynchronously, serves users, depends on external systems, or must be diagnosed after execution.
required_evidence: Structured queryable debug, info, warn, and error records cover material transitions, dependency boundaries, retries, and failures.
Records carry stable event and operation names, time, component, environment, release or build, outcome, and safe correlation as applicable.

Handled and unhandled errors preserve bounded class, cause chain, stack, impact, retryability, and safe context; exact-artifact source maps or debug symbols resolve compiled or minified stacks where applicable.
obligations.exception_authority: Accountable project owner; a local-only utility may use bounded local structured records when no remote operation exists.

obligations.title: Authoritative product activity
obligations.applies_when: The project promises a user or operator journey whose completion cannot be inferred from uptime or error absence.
required_evidence: A versioned first-party schema covers material success, rejection or failure, abandonment, and recovery transitions.
Each event has one semantic owner, identity and deduplication rule, source and occurrence time, schema version, environment, release, outcome, and safe correlation.
Accepted and completed states use server or durable receipt authority where available; client-only observations are labeled.
obligations.exception_authority: Accountable product owner with an explicit substitute for the promised-journey decision; no blanket waiver from private deployment alone.

obligations.title: Safe and bounded operational data
obligations.applies_when: The project emits diagnostics, errors, traces, metrics, or product activity.
required_evidence: Producer-side typed allowlists exclude secrets, credentials, authorization values, cookies, raw headers or bodies, arbitrary user content, prompts, messages, and stack locals by default.
Identity scope, pseudonymization, consent or approved basis, user choice, deletion, tenant isolation, retention, access, region, cardinality, volume, cost, and sampling have owners and bounds.
A slow or failed sink cannot fail or stall the product path or recurse; bounded buffer, retry, or drop behavior exposes loss or backpressure independently.
obligations.exception_authority: Security or privacy owner plus accountable project owner; any narrow content capture states purpose, access boundary, approval, and deletion policy.

obligations.title: Executed observability proof
required_evidence: Representative success and every material failure journey assert shape, level, correlation, authority, cause, release attribution, and single emission or deduplication.
Negative canaries prove secrets and content do not leave the producer; controlled failures prove useful error capture, source resolution where applicable, and product survival during sink outage.
A fresh sanitized record is retrieved from the intended sink; SDK presence or schema syntax alone is not runtime coverage.
obligations.exception_authority: Accountable project owner with the exact unproved runtime boundary and a time-bounded production-readiness condition.

obligations.title: Owned operational use
obligations.applies_when: An emitted signal is claimed to support a material failure response or product decision.
required_evidence: Each material failure and product decision has a documented query or dashboard, freshness and retention expectation, owner, and response.
Alerts are actionable and define condition, window, destination, recovery behavior, direct diagnostic query, and runbook.
A controlled failure-and-recovery retrieval is exercised before coverage is claimed.
obligations.exception_authority: Accountable operations or product owner with the decision explicitly removed or a named substitute query and response path.

obligations.title: First-class project documents
obligations.applies_when: The repository is maintained as a project.
required_evidence: Root README.md, AGENTS.md, DOMAIN.md with its invariants ledger, and USER_STORIES.md own orientation, operating instructions, boundaries and user intent; every repository has an executable scripts/check invoked by CI.

Surface-specific evidence: DESIGN.md for ui, a Release/Rollback/Recover runbook for deployed, a content schema and lint for content; ADRs, when present, have unique numbers, status and resolvable supersessions under docs/adr/.

Aliases are symlinks to AGENTS.md; core Markdown links and AGENTS routing commands resolve at HEAD. A committed .env.pass, when present, contains names-only credential references. Other generated references and the public face remain follow-up checks (ADR-004).
obligations.exception_authority: Accountable project owner with a documented substitute for the missing project record.

obligations.title: Navigable feature map
obligations.applies_when: The project has live user stories and tracked implementation sources.
required_evidence: features/README.md indexes feature files with live story IDs and tracked source globs.
Every live story is mapped, and each feature records sub-features, user entry, driving procedure, and gotchas.
obligations.exception_authority: Accountable product owner with an explicit alternative mapping from live stories to sources.

obligations.title: Story-walk receipts
obligations.applies_when: A change affects a mapped story or story definition.
required_evidence: A same-job walk receipt binds the candidate head and tree and passes every affected story and criterion.
Every cited evidence artifact has a retained path and matching digest; unwalked stories stay advisory only with a current walk: baseline and never count as passing.
obligations.exception_authority: Accountable project owner with an independently reviewed, time-bounded substitute walk.

obligations.title: Workspace-ready bootstrap
obligations.applies_when: Every active repository (ADR-004): checks run in a fresh Ubuntu LTS exe.dev VM and GitHub-hosted Ubuntu runner.
required_evidence: .exe/setup.sh is credential-free and idempotent in both a fresh Ubuntu LTS exe.dev VM and GitHub-hosted Ubuntu runner.
Bootstrap installs or configures the toolchain required for the project's checks without desktop credentials.
obligations.exception_authority: Accountable project owner with an equivalent reproducible, credential-free workspace bootstrap.

obligations.title: Independent review against project judgement rules
obligations.applies_when: Every change to a maintained repository.
required_evidence: A reviewer other than the PR author approves the candidate head after examining the Foundation constitution, the invariants ledger at the base revision, and the story the change serves.
The repository's review gate checks an independent approving review on the head; only the review receipt shows the actual judgement against the constitution, base ledger and story.
obligations.exception_authority: Designated reviewer under ADR-003, with a time-bounded substitute independent review.

obligations.title: Security baseline
obligations.applies_when: Secret scanning and dependency maintenance apply to every active repository; authorization-boundary tests additionally apply to applications (ui, cli, api or deployed).
required_evidence: The gate runs a named secret-scanning workflow job on PRs and pushes; a configured dependency bot proposes current dependencies, and a green-gated auto-merge job restricts merges to bot patch and minor updates.
Applications name an authorization test and the workflow job that runs it, including a denied and an allowed case.

The checker resolves configured files, workflow jobs, job dependencies and test references. Only a receipt can show the scan ran, updates were safely merged, and authorization was exercised with meaningful identities.
obligations.exception_authority: Designated reviewer and security owner with residual risk and an expiring substitute control.

obligations.title: Affected-story citation
obligations.applies_when: A pull request changes source mapped to live stories in a feature map.
required_evidence: The pull request description cites every affected live story id returned by foundation-check affected --base <base> for mapped source changes, in a Stories: US-001, US-002 line.

The review gate computes affected ids from the PR's base and candidate head and compares them with the description; the story's actual relevance and implementation are judged in review and the walk receipt.
obligations.exception_authority: Designated reviewer with an explanation of an unmapped change and a dated mapping gap.

obligations.title: Continuous deployment
obligations.applies_when: The repository is an application: it changes a live system (surface deployed) or ships something people run (surfaces ui, cli or api).
required_evidence: Every push to the default branch that passes the gate deploys to production automatically, whether the trunk is named main, master or otherwise: a deploy or release job waits on the gate, runs with no manual step, and a failed gate stops it.

The gate is strong enough to ship at 5pm on a Friday: CI, automated tests of the core journeys, story walks and agentic QA run before shipping, and a readback or smoke check verifies the shipped candidate.
Rollback or recovery of a bad release is exercised, and recent default-branch history shows green commits reaching production without hand steps.
For a multi-tenant application, the deploy reaches every tenant in its complete registry; the receipt reads back every non-excluded tenant after deploy.
Any tenant excluded from the multi-tenant rollout is explicitly named in the adoption record with a non-empty reason; an exclusion is a reviewable record change, not an implicit deploy filter.
Before deployment, migrations run for each non-excluded tenant, remain backward-compatible with the still-running code (expand/contract), and a failed tenant migration stops the rollout.
The repository can report every tenant's production state, including each tenant's deployed revision and migration level, with excluded tenants still visible.
obligations.exception_authority: None. Operator decision 2026-09-25 (ADR-005): no exception for an application; not_applicable only when the repository is not an application.

obligations.title: Loud production alerting
obligations.applies_when: The repository is an application: it changes a live system (surface deployed) or ships something people run (surfaces ui, cli or api).
required_evidence: Production errors are captured remotely with release and environment: Sentry by default (FND-DEF-SENTRY-001) or an approved equivalent that captures errors, checks health and raises incidents.
Health is checked from outside the application on a schedule; a released artifact without a live service instead reports crashes and errors from real installs.
Errors and failed health checks alert loudly only to an approved agent triage intake, never a person's inbox or phone; a controlled failure proves the alert was seen and handled.
For Sentry, every alert rule's actions target the approved intake, and no alert email goes to organization members.
obligations.exception_authority: None. Operator decision 2026-09-25 (ADR-005): no exception for an application; not_applicable only when the repository is not an application.

obligations.title: Incident response closes the class
obligations.applies_when: The repository is an application: it changes a live system (surface deployed) or ships something people run (surfaces ui, cli or api).
required_evidence: The runbook's Incidents section says how an alert becomes an owned incident, who responds, and where its postmortem goes.
The triage agent reads each alert, opens the incident ticket, and starts an engineer or escalates to Kaylee only when the alert is real.
Every production incident ends in a postmortem under docs/postmortems/ from the harness template in the pokayoke skill.

An incident ticket closes only with the postmortem it links and the structural change that postmortem links to rule out the whole class of error (shape, type, ownership, a removed affordance or a failing-closed check), together with its regression check; a warning or instruction is not a fix.
obligations.exception_authority: None. Operator decision 2026-09-25 (ADR-005): no exception for an application; not_applicable only when the repository is not an application.

approved_defaults.applies_when: A Misty Step user-facing application or operated service needs remote error capture and has no approved equivalent.
approved_defaults.default: Use Sentry for error capture, environment and release association, and source-map or debug-symbol processing.
approved_defaults.override_authority: Accountable project owner may name an existing equivalent that satisfies the same applicable obligations; record the choice in the adoption manifest.

approved_defaults.applies_when: A product journey needs activity evidence and the project already owns a suitable durable store.
approved_defaults.default: Use a minimal versioned first-party event table in the existing store, including D1 or Convex where those are already the project store, before adding another analytics platform.
approved_defaults.override_authority: Accountable product owner may approve another owned platform with equivalent authority, privacy, deletion, retrieval, and deduplication behavior.

pending_requires: unexpired baseline gap obl:<ID> for every applicable pending obligation
satisfied_requires: untracked foundation/receipts/*.json with foundation-evidence/1 schema, obligation, HEAD revision, check, run, exit 0, path and sha256 of the retained payload in the same receipt directory
approval_record_requires: tracked foundation/approvals/*.json at HEAD with schema, obligation, disposition, reason, substitute and matching exception expiry if applicable
designated reviewer approval of the introducing or amended record on the PR head
exception_policy.review_trigger: Reassess when project capability, data scope, hosting, or release path changes.
exception_policy.trust_boundary: The checker verifies receipt bytes and record shape; GitHub review authenticates the approver. Committed names, approvals and receipts cannot prove the underlying runtime practice or review substance.
